title: stake() is not poolState-gated, so any ERC1155 holder can block finalizeAndReset and wedge the in-place migration
description: `stake` carries no poolState guard, so a stake during `Migrating` makes `totalStaked > 0` and reverts `finalizeAndReset`'s `require(totalStaked == 0)`. `finalizeAndReset` is the ONLY transition back to Active and `depositFor` requires Active, so this blocks `InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn` for every other parked user for as long as the staking continues.
impact: Two impacts. (1) AVAILABILITY: finalizeAndReset requires totalStaked == 0 and is the ONLY transition back to Active; depositFor requires Active. A single permissionless stake during Migrating therefore blocks InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.migrateIn for EVERY other parked user, for as long as the staking continues. (2) SILENT USER VALUE LOSS: accRewardPerShare is frozen during Migrating, so the contract ACCEPTS a stake it will never pay on — pendingReward == 0 is asserted in the PoC. The staker is not warned and not refused.
attackPath: 1. Operator calls initiateMigration; poolState becomes Migrating.
2. Any holder of the ERC1155 calls stake() — ungated, permissionless, a legitimate documented user action.
4. The pool cannot return to Active, so no parked user can be migrated in.
5. ECON-02's 6-step PoC shows the re-park re-arms the timeout clock, so the loop repeats.
6. The staker who did it earns nothing — the position accrues against a frozen accRewardPerShare.
likelihood: medium-to-high, and MORE LIKELY ACCIDENTAL THAN ADVERSARIAL — the timeout hatch and the stake button are both legitimate documented user actions, so an ordinary user can wedge the migration without intending to. Pure-cost griefing with zero attacker profit.
assumptions: The pool is in Migrating and at least one ERC1155 unit is outside the migrator's custody.
justification: C4 Medium: assets are not at direct risk, but the availability of a core protocol operation (the in-place migration) is impacted by an unprivileged action, and a second leg silently costs an uninvolved user their yield for the duration. Escalated from the scanner's Low per D-10; the dedup record pre-authorised a `medium` severityCeiling. The sanctioned 'pause first' remedy is PROVEN COMPLETE by execution (PoC_Local001 testPauseRemedyIsComplete: stake/unstake/claim are whenNotPaused while every migration primitive and every user escape remains callable while paused) — but that remedy carries an ecosystem-wide halt cost, filed separately as CLASS-014. A remedy that costs a whole-ecosystem outage is not a reason to call the defect Low.
recommendation: Add require(poolState == PoolState.Active) to stake(). Free, behaviour-preserving, and removes the need to reach for the ecosystem-wide pause at all.
